headline: Nvidia's 5.86% Slide Sets a Wary Tone as Chip Selloff Meets a Holiday-Shortened Week
body_html:
Nvidia heads into Wednesday's open on the back foot after falling 5.86% on Tuesday, a move that shifted more market value than any other company's. The drop came as worries about AI spending returned: credit-default-swap spreads on several AI-linked borrowers reportedly hit records. The stock is also on track for its worst month since 2022. President Trump floated a US government stake in the company and a pardon for chief executive Jensen Huang, but the shares failed to hold any lift. Singapore's prime minister also criticised US cooperation in a probe involving Nvidia chips.

The damage spread across the sector. Semiconductors fell an average of 7.69%, with Micron down 11.01%, AMD down 8.86%, Broadcom down 3.98% and TSMC down 3.96%. The S&P 500 slipped 0.49% and the Nasdaq lost 1.99%. Beneath the surface the market was mixed: 372 stocks rose and 289 fell, as healthcare and consumer discretionary names gained.

At the open, watch whether chip stocks stabilise or extend the slide, and how traders react to the day's inflation reading after the dollar firmed overnight. Thursday is a market holiday, and Friday's session ends at 1:00 p.m. ET, so liquidity may thin.

briefs.headline: Smaller chip names take the harshest hits
briefs.body: Beyond the giants, the selloff hit smaller semiconductor firms hardest. Ambarella fell 19.96%, Semtech 16.97% and MaxLinear 16.74%, while Ichor lost 16.49%. Connectivity names Astera Labs and Credo dropped 13.88% and 13.07%. Watch for any bounce, or further pressure, at the open.

briefs.headline: Micron sinks 11.01% after downgrade
briefs.body: Micron fell 11.01% after it ran into a price ceiling and drew an analyst downgrade, according to market commentary. AMD fell 8.86% alongside it. Traders will want to see whether memory stocks find buyers or the AI-chip pullback keeps feeding on itself.

briefs.headline: TSMC weighs export curbs and tariff talk
briefs.body: TSMC slipped 3.96% as investors weighed new export curbs and Trump's warning of steep future tariffs on chips. Reports tie those tariff threats to the company's Texas plant plans, which hinge on two tax breaks. Policy headlines may keep foundry shares volatile.

briefs.headline: Healthcare and retail provide the offset
briefs.body: Healthcare rose an average of 2.56% and consumer discretionary 1.88%. Abercrombie & Fitch jumped 19.69% and Dick's Sporting Goods 14.59%. Sanofi gained 10.97% and MiniMed 14.09%. Apple rose 1.43%, one of the few large technology names in the green.

briefs.headline: Dollar firms ahead of inflation data
briefs.body: The dollar rallied before a key US inflation reading, with the Australian dollar and sterling slumping. Gold slipped on the stronger currency, and oil fell more than 1% as supply-glut prospects outweighed Middle East disruption fears. The data print is the main scheduled catalyst today.

briefs.headline: Holiday calendar shapes the week
briefs.body: With Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday closing US markets, today is the last full session of the week. Friday trades only until 1:00 p.m. ET. Shortened schedules can mean thinner volume and sharper moves, particularly in chip stocks already under pressure.
